details:
Wander Nauta discovered that Erlang incorrectly handled absolute paths when
extracting zip archives. An attacker could possibly use this issue to write
arbitrary files outside of the intended directory. This issue only affected
Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-4748)

It was discovered that the Erlang SFTP server did not properly limit the
size of packets. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause
Erlang to use excessive resources, leading to a denial of service. This
issue only affected Ubuntu 14.04 LTS, Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, and
Ubuntu 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-26618)

It was discovered that the Erlang SSH server did not properly limit the
length of algorithm names in key exchange messages. A remote attacker could
possibly use this issue to cause Erlang to use excessive resources, leading
to a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 14.04 LTS,
Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-30211)

It was discovered that the Erlang TFTP server incorrectly handled certain
file paths. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to access files
outside of the intended directory. (CVE-2026-21620)

It was discovered that the Erlang SFTP server incorrectly validated paths
against the configured root directory. An authenticated user could possibly
use this issue to access files outside of the root directory.
(CVE-2026-23942)

It was discovered that the Erlang SSH server enabled zlib compression by
default and did not limit the size of decompressed data. A remote attacker
could possibly use this issue to cause Erlang to use excessive resources,
leading to a denial of service. (CVE-2026-23943)

It was discovered that the Erlang HTTP server incorrectly applied directory
access controls to CGI scripts served via script aliases. A remote attacker
could possibly use this issue to bypass authentication and access protected
CGI scripts. (CVE-2026-28808)

It was discovered that the Erlang DNS resolver used predictable transaction
IDs and did not randomize source ports. A remote attacker could possibly
use this issue to perform DNS cache poisoning attacks. This issue only
affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS.
(CVE-2026-28810)

It was discovered that Erlang did not verify the signatures of designated
OCSP responder certificates. A remote attacker could possibly use this
issue to forge OCSP responses and bypass certificate revocation checks.
This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-32144)

It was discovered that the Erlang SFTP server incorrectly handled file
attribute changes on open file handles. An authenticated user could
possibly use this issue to modify the attributes of files outside of the
root directory. (CVE-2026-32147)

It was discovered that Erlang incorrectly allowed non-CA certificates to
act as intermediate certificate issuers. A remote attacker could possibly
use this issue to forge certificate chains. (CVE-2026-42789)

It was discovered that Erlang incorrectly handled DNS name constraints
during hostname verification. A remote attacker could possibly use this
issue to bypass certificate validation. This issue only affected
Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, and
Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-42790)

It was discovered that Erlang did not check the validity period of OCSP
responder certificates. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to
forge OCSP responses using an expired responder certificate. This issue
only affected Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-42791)

It was discovered that Erlang incorrectly handled relative paths when
extracting zip archives. An attacker could possibly use this issue to write
arbitrary files outside of the intended directory. This issue only affected
Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, and
Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-47078)

It was discovered that the Erlang SFTP server exposed absolute paths when
reading symbolic links. An authenticated user could possibly use this issue
to obtain sensitive information. (CVE-2026-48855)

It was discovered that the Erlang HTTP client forwarded authorization
headers on cross-origin redirects. A malicious HTTP server could possibly
use this issue to obtain sensitive information. (CVE-2026-48856)

It was discovered that the Erlang FTP client did not validate the IP
address in passive mode responses. A malicious FTP server could possibly
use this issue to perform server-side request forgery attacks.
(CVE-2026-48858)

It was discovered that Erlang checked the local address instead of the peer
address when enforcing the allowlist for distribution over TLS. A remote
attacker could possibly use this issue to bypass access restrictions. This
issue only affected Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-48860)

It was discovered that Erlang incorrectly handled certain SCTP ERROR
chunks, leading to a buffer overflow. A remote attacker could possibly use
this issue to cause Erlang to crash, resulting in a denial of service.
(CVE-2026-49759)

It was discovered that the Erlang erl_interface library incorrectly handled
printing very large integers, leading to a buffer overflow. An attacker
could possibly use this issue to cause Erlang to crash or execute arbitrary
code. (CVE-2026-49760)

It was discovered that the Erlang SFTP server incorrectly handled certain
path resolution requests. An authenticated user could possibly use this
issue to determine the existence of files outside of the root directory.
(CVE-2026-53422)

It was discovered that the Erlang SFTP server incorrectly handled extended
channel data, leading to an infinite loop. An authenticated user could
possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2026-54886)

It was discovered that the Erlang DTLS server used a predictable cookie
secret on startup. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to
bypass source address verification. This issue only affected
Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, and
Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-54887)

It was discovered that Erlang TLS clients incorrectly accepted application
data before the handshake was completed. A remote attacker could possibly
use this issue to inject arbitrary data into TLS connections.
(CVE-2026-54891)

It was discovered that the Erlang DTLS server contained a race condition
when handling rapid client reconnections. A remote attacker could possibly
use this issue to cause Erlang to crash, resulting in a denial of service.
This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS.
(CVE-2026-55950)

It was discovered that Erlang did not properly validate TLS 1.3 pre-shared
key extensions. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause
Erlang to crash, resulting in a denial of service. This issue only affected
Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS.
(CVE-2026-55952)

It was discovered that the Erlang ASN.1 decoder incorrectly handled certain
object identifiers. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to
cause Erlang to use excessive resources, leading to a denial of service.
(CVE-2026-65634)

It was discovered that the Erlang SSH server did not properly limit the
number of open channels. An authenticated user could possibly use this
issue to cause Erlang to use excessive resources, leading to a denial of
service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS,
Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS.
(CVE-2026-68956)

It was discovered that the Erlang HTTP server incorrectly shared users and
groups between directories when using dets or mnesia authentication
backends. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to bypass
authentication and access protected directories. (CVE-2026-74994)

It was discovered that Erlang TLS clients incorrectly accepted unsolicited
TLS 1.3 pre-shared keys from servers. A remote attacker could possibly use
this issue to impersonate servers. This issue only affected
Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS.
(CVE-2026-89422)
